raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. Money is tight, and with people going out for work, I mostly do what is steady and familiar. On the better part of the land, 2.6 mu, I keep the wheat-maize rotation because that gives grain from two seasons and feels safer. The other 1.5 mu I keep in cotton, because if the price is decent it brings cash, even though it takes more watching. I do not like making big changes. If the land looked weak last year, I give a bit more fertilizer, but I still count every yuan. I have well water, so if it turns dry I can save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not water for nothing.

For wheat, I sow in early October like people here usually do, with local improved seed that I can get nearby. Before sowing I put on a base dressing, not too little because wheat without base fertilizer has weak seedlings. Then at jointing, if the leaves are pale, I topdress again and give water. After wheat harvest in June, I do not waste time because the maize must go in fast. I usually clear the straw quickly, scratch the soil shallow, and plant maize right away. Maize I keep simple: decent hybrid seed, one base fertilizer pass, one topdress when it grows fast, and one irrigation if the summer rain is not enough. Cotton is different. It is slower money, but if I manage insects and keep the field clean, it can still help the household. I will not push cotton too hard with expensive inputs; I will feed it enough, water it a couple of times, and spray only when I really see trouble.
